Research on misinformation, political economy, and environmental governance.

## Journal articles

```{=html}
<div class="work-list"><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2026 · Cambridge Journal of Artificial Intelligence</p><h3><a href="/publications/epistemic_frontier_capitalism/">The Epistemic Frontier of Capitalism: A Theory of Epistemic Regression through Artificial Intelligence and Misinformation</a></h3><p>This article argues that contemporary capitalism has entered a phase in which outcomes are increasingly shaped by the privatization and strategic destabilization of the epistemic commons through frontier artificial intelligence and platform-mediated misinformation.</p><a class="text-link" href="/publications/epistemic_frontier_capitalism/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2026 · Review of Evolutionary Political Economy</p><h3><a href="/publications/liberal_order_complex_societies_climate_change/">The Liberal Order in Complex Societies Marred by Climate Change</a></h3><p>This essay develops a complexity-oriented research program for classical liberal thought, showing how rule-of-law institutions can enable cooperation amid political, economic, and environmental pressures from climate change.</p><a class="text-link" href="/publications/liberal_order_complex_societies_climate_change/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2026 · PLOS Climate</p><h3><a href="/publications/Beyond_post_truth_climate_misinformation/">Beyond Post-Truth: Projecting the Future Trajectory of Climate Misinformation</a></h3><p>Climate misinformation represents one of the most significant barriers to effective climate action in the 21st century. Building upon Yotam Ophir’s framework, this essay examines how climate misinformation is evolving and projects its future trajectory.</p><a class="text-link" href="/publications/Beyond_post_truth_climate_misinformation/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2026 · Journal of Libertarian Studies</p><h3><a href="/publications/misinformation_challenge_information_freedom/">The Misinformation Challenge: How Information Freedom Promotes Democratic Discourse</a></h3><p>The contemporary discourse surrounding misinformation has generated unprecedented calls for government intervention in information markets and content regulation. This article argues that decentralized information governance, market competition, and robust protections for free expression offer a stronger democratic response than top-down content controls.</p><a class="text-link" href="/publications/misinformation_challenge_information_freedom/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2025 · Cambridge Journal of Climate Research</p><h3><a href="/publications/Knowledge_asymmetries_climate_finance/">Knowledge Asymmetries and Climate Finance: An Inquiry into Environmental Market Failures and Political Legitimacy</a></h3><p>In archetypal credit and capital markets, informational gaps can lead to the withdrawal of high-impact participants and incentivise excessive risk-taking by parties unaware of the risks they face. Within climate-related markets there is a similar trend: investors systematically underestimate tail risks associated with carbon-intensive assets—including risks from climate-caused natural events, which threaten those assets—while firms strategically under-disclose their exposure to these physical and transition risks.</p><a class="text-link" href="/publications/Knowledge_asymmetries_climate_finance/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2024 · Cambridge Journal of Climate Research</p><h3><a href="/publications/Just_emissions/">The Prospect of ‘Just Emissions’ as an International Norm of Environmental Governance</a></h3><p>So-called luxury emissions of Global North countries need to be curtailed in line with, and also more rapidly than, the increase in emissions from Global South nations. I argue there is a growing need for radical social austerity and climate conservatism on the part of large emitters.</p><a class="text-link" href="/publications/Just_emissions/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article></div>
```

Evidence from Social Media and Firm-Level Data</a></h3><p>This paper combines social media analytics with corporate performance data to test how misinformation surrounding climate change influences firms' ESG outcomes.</p><a class="text-link" href="/working_papers/climate_misinformation_esg/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2025 · Working Paper</p><h3><a href="/working_papers/liberal_complexity/">Climate Change and Complexity in Classical Liberal Theories of Development</a></h3><p>In this essay, I develop a complexity-based theory of social interaction within legal constraints, highlighting how rule-of-law institutions enable cooperation even in the face of intricate political and economic pressures based on inequities in mitigating and preparing for climate change..</p><a class="text-link" href="/working_papers/liberal_complexity/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2025 · Under Review at <i>Political Theology</i></p><h3><a href="/working_papers/religious_political_neutrality/">To What Extent Are Religious Political Actors Constrained by Political Neutrality?</a></h3><p>This article examines doctrinal debates about neutrality to assess how religious actors navigate political advocacy in pluralist democracies.</p><a class="text-link" href="/working_papers/religious_political_neutrality/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2025 · Working paper with Charles Mensah</p><h3><a href="/working_papers/Sustainable_business/">Interdisciplinarity in International Sustainable Business</a></h3><p>This essay proposes that international business - characterized most prominently by the multinational corporation (MNC) - is defined by the types of social problems it wishes to solve. It is also defined by the manner, strategy, or approach that it uses to define the problem landscape and technological or product-related solution space.</p><a class="text-link" href="/working_papers/Sustainable_business/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2024 · Working Paper</p><h3><a href="/working_papers/religious_political_morality/">The Social Construction of Religious Political Morality</a></h3><p>This is my LSE dissertation. It is currently a conference paper, as I prepare for publication.</p><a class="text-link" href="/working_papers/religious_political_morality/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2024 · Working Paper</p><h3><a href="/working_papers/Climate_Misinformation/">The Social Justification of Climate Change Beliefs and Environmental Communication</a></h3><p>While our beliefs about crucial political issues such as climate change are shaped by a variety of psychological and socioeconomic influences, this essay argues that one source of those beliefs comes from the responsibility that climate scientists have, as domain experts on the science and policy of climate change, to protect the public from misinformation.</p><a class="text-link" href="/working_papers/Climate_Misinformation/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article><article class="work-card"><p class="eyebrow">2024 · Science & Religion Forum 2024 Conference</p><h3><a href="/working_papers/ecological_ethics/">An Ecological Ethics for the Anthropocene: Environmental Justice and Religion</a></h3><p>This essay examines the relationship between critical theological theories within avant-garde scholarship on religion as a social phenomenon and the equally, if not more, pressing revelations of climate scientists regarding the ecological crisis which is partly the result of a society whose faith has been misplaced in a form of unsustainable technology which threatens to destroy us.</p><a class="text-link" href="/working_papers/ecological_ethics/">Read more <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></article></div>
